business_scope: Table grape export market trends, European shipping windows, residue compliance economics, and domestic market strategies.

crop_business_factors.details: Table grapes exported to European and Middle Eastern markets between January and April capture maximum realisations. Unexported batches diverted to local mandis suffer heavy discounting.
Strict maximum residue limits (MRL) dictate market access; compliance is mandatory for entering high-value export retail supply chains.

common_risks.details: Rain events close to harvest cause berry splitting and fungal decay, instantly destroying export-grade market value.

market_factors.details: During severe domestic market gluts or export rejections, converting surplus table grapes into raisins serves as a risk-mitigation strategy.

cost_factors: Export-grade corrugated packaging and air/shipping logistics
revenue_factors: Percentage of marketable yield meeting strict size and Brix requirements
cost_revenue_factors.important_rule: Grape marketing success is defined by strict adherence to export quality specifications and timely shipping logistics.

strengths: Established cooperative export logistics infrastructure in Maharashtra.
weaknesses: Zero tolerance for pesticide residues in target export markets.
opportunities: Diversifying into emerging non-traditional export destinations.
threats: Unpredictable hailstorms and severe European market price competition.

things_to_monitor: European import demand forecasts and container shipping rates
Pre-harvest safety intervals for pesticide applications
Local mandi price trends as a fallback option
